dominant_cause: Source-currency pin drift.  19 failures name `source_current` outright and the `test_retained_*_is_bound_to_these_sources` family accounts for most of the rest: a certificate records the SHA-256 of an input, the input has since moved, and the producer refuses rather than regenerating silently.  That is the pins working as designed on a tree whose artifacts were not re-taken, not a code defect.

how_the_comparison_was_done_and_the_trap.how_it_was_settled_without_the_worktree: By digest, in the main checkout.  The failing pin is `results/abi3/rom_schedule_checks.json.source.campaign_tool`, which records e9ab077a... for tools/check_rom_schedules.py while the file hashes 49a6d5d1...  Both the tool AND the certificate are BYTE-IDENTICAL at d995c8b and at HEAD -- `git diff d995c8b HEAD` on the certificate is empty and `git show <rev>:<tool>` hashes the same both ways -- so the mismatch exists at both revisions and cannot be caused by any commit between them.  The tool's last commit is b8ec2db, five days before this session.
how_the_comparison_was_done_and_the_trap.method: The same suite run in a worktree at d995c8b -- the commit before this session's first -- and the FAILING NAME SETS compared.
how_the_comparison_was_done_and_the_trap.the_trap: A worktree carries neither build/ nor the ignored fixtures, so every test gated on `skipif(not _deployment_bundles_present())` is SKIPPED there.  A skip prints no FAILED line, so set-differencing 'failed at head' against 'failed at base' reads a skip as a PASS.  Three tests looked like regressions of mine for exactly that reason: test_a_lowered_work_bound_bounds_both_sides, test_deployment_target_certificates_match_every_current_input and test_deployment_vector_set_is_reproducible.
